text:

His conviction in the way he lives, his ability to bring people together and his willingness to extend grace when it is needed set him apart. He creates an environment where people feel supported, included and encouraged to become the best versions of themselves. Eli alone makes any experience ten times better, regardless of the destination, and I would travel anywhere with him as a leader.

Nikki brought an entirely different and equally valuable energy to the trip. She made everything more fun while also having a remarkable ability to make everyone feel comfortable being completely themselves. From creating TikTok music videos and laughing over the smallest things to having meaningful one-on-one conversations, she knew exactly when to bring the energy and when to slow down and genuinely connect.

Nikki was also one of the best yoga instructors I have ever practiced with. Meditation and journaling have always been difficult for me, but her guidance made both feel natural, accessible and meaningful. She leads with kindness, and that kindness speaks volumes. Nothing about her approach felt forced or performative. She created a safe space that allowed people to open up, reflect and participate at their own pace.

Together, Eli and Nikki created the perfect balance of adventure, structure, laughter, reflection and genuine connection. They made every person feel seen and brought out something special in the entire group. I would enthusiastically book another trip led by either of them and would be especially excited to travel with them together again.

This was more than an incredible vacation. It was a life changing experience, and Nikki and Eli were a huge reason why.

name: Lyndsay Hern
text:
My husband and I just returned from Surf Yoga Beer’s first Côte d’Azur, French Riviera trip, and we honestly can’t say enough good things about the experience.

We originally booked this trip to support our longtime friend Erin, one of the trip leaders. Going into it, we really didn’t know what to expect. We knew these types of group travel experiences tend to attract more solo (and often single) travelers, so as a couple we weren’t sure how we’d fit in.

From the moment we arrived, every single one of the people on the trip made us feel welcomed, included, and genuinely loved. By the end of the week, it felt like we had gained an entire new group of friends.

The itinerary was definitely go, go, go! If we had one small piece of feedback, it would be to build in a little more downtime at some beaches to relax and soak it all in. That said, we’re both very active and social people, so we loved how much we were able to experience.

Our welcome dinner the first night in Cassis was incredible—a family-style seafood feast with so many amazing dishes to try.

The kayaking adventure through the Calanques was one of our favorite experiences. We had never been kayaking before, and now we can’t wait to do it again. The scenery was absolutely breathtaking.

In Castellane at Verdon Gorge, we went canyoning for the first time. We’ve floated the American River before, so we thought we knew what to expect…we were very wrong! It was much more adventurous than anticipated, but so much fun. Our guide did an incredible job making everyone feel safe and comfortable throughout the experience. I may have been shivering for the entire hour and a half because the water was freezing (LOL), but it was absolutely worth it.

The lavender field photo shoot was another unforgettable highlight. Even though we had some crazy wind, the fields were stunning, and Matas somehow managed to capture absolutely gorgeous photos despite the conditions.

Our bike tour through Saint-Tropez was another favorite. We only wish we had more time to explore the town because we completely fell in love with it. Between the beautiful beaches, an amazing lunch, and winery visit, it was an incredible day that ended with an amazing group dinner at Crazy Pizza.

The four leaders absolutely made this trip what it was. Erin has been one of my best friends since high school, so I already knew how amazing she is. But watching her lead a large group was incredible. Whether she was leading a killer morning yoga session, planning an unforgettable SHELLONA beach club day (which was one of the highlights of the trip, and for being a “free night” all 27 of us went and it was worth the cost!), or being the first one ready to celebrate and have fun at night, she brought such an authentic, positive energy that made everyone want to have fun.

Christian was pure positivity from start to finish. His energy is genuinely contagious. From 7 a.m. workouts to turning every bus ride into a dance party, he had everyone laughing, singing, and smiling. He has a way of making every single person feel included, and that kind of leadership is something special.

Matas was our incredible photographer, and we are so grateful he was there to capture memories we’ll have forever. Beyond his talent behind the camera, he’s one of the most genuine, down-to-earth people we’ve met. It was awesome getting to know him when he wasn’t busy documenting the adventure.

Holly was equally amazing. She constantly made an effort to connect with everyone, made people feel welcome, and led some fun workouts. Her encouragement and chill vibes never went unnoticed.

If you ever have the opportunity to join a trip with Erin, Holly, Christian, and Matas, consider yourself lucky. They created an environment where complete strangers became friends and where everyone truly felt like they belonged.

This was our first Surf Yoga Beer trip, and it absolutely won’t be our last. We have nothing else to compare it to, but if this is the standard, we can’t wait to book another adventure.

If you’re on the fence, don’t overthink it.

name: Jeniffer Miranda
text:
I don’t say this lightly - my Surf Yoga Beer trip to the Philippines was unlike anything I’ve ever experienced!  That’s saying a lot, even compared to other SYB trips I’ve been on.
Palawan is truly a hidden gem, it’s one of those places you don’t even realize is missing from your bucket list until you’re there, completely in awe.  The experience with TAO, and the incredible TAO boys, made it even more special.  They took care of everything from navigating the boat expedition to setting up our beach huts to sleep in each night and of course keeping us well fed with delicious, freshly made meals (and plenty of jungle juice).  Their local knowledge, high energy, and ability to create fun out of every moment took the whole adventure to another level.
What really made this trip unforgettable though were our leaders, Lizzie and Ryan.  You could feel how much intention they put into curating an experience that fostered genuine connection.  The nature of the trip already sets the stage with no cell service, no distractions, stripped down from the “real world” (goodbye makeup and hot showers), and instead you’re placed on remote, breathtaking beaches surrounded by incredible people.  Yet somehow Lizzie and Ryan elevated it even more.  Their excitement for leading workouts, sunset yoga, mindful moments, and themed parties was contagious.  They created a space where everyone felt comfortable being their most authentic selves, something that seems rare these days.  Also, a special shoutout to Ryan for capturing everyone’s best moments through candid photos, I’m talking frame-worthy memories from the trip of a lifetime.
This may not be SYB’s most well-known trip but honestly, it should be!  It perfectly balances movement, adventure, and meaningful social connection in a setting that feels almost unreal.  You leave not just with memories, but with a true sense of belonging, to nature, to the people you met, and to the SYB community as a whole.
If you weren’t considering this trip before, I hope you are now… and if you need one more reason here it is: Lizzie is leading this trip again in 2027!  Don’t miss it.

name: Julian Pedraza
text:
I did an extensive search for surf camps across Central America and was lucky to find SYB Nicaragua as one of the most promising options. Mantas, the owner, kindly explained how it worked and shared experiences from previous guests. That’s when I realized I was getting more than I expected—a balanced mix of surfing, wellness, and active living, surrounded by people with similar lifestyles. I was there in the middle of March.

Carri and Rob are excellent hosts and leaders. They unite the team, guide everyone, and join right in. Drawing on insights from past trips, they keep improving the experience for each new group. Their great reputation across the villas, beach, and town helps guests connect easily with locals, making everything enjoyable and stress-free. My understanding is hosts rotate for every trip.

The trip lasted six days, with two spent mainly traveling from Liberia, Costa Rica to San Juan del Sur and back. If possible, fly directly to Managua—you’ll save several hours and avoid border hassles.

We surfed three of the four active days, doing one to two sessions per day. Alongside that, we had guided yoga, training, journaling, town explorations, and visits to bars and restaurants—a well-balanced mix of activities. I won’t spoil the details, but it was amazing!

All the locals working with SYB, from drivers and chefs to surf instructors, guides and others, were friendly, helpful, and easy to connect with. Building personal bonds with them was probably the most fulfilling part. The food at the villas was incredible, you’ll wish you could take the cooks home!

My fellow solo travelers were exceptional, coming from all corners of the US. We had an ideal balance of ages, professions, and routines, and spending time together helped us form close bonds.

You know a trip was great when you don’t want to return to reality. it’s been a month, and I still wish I was there.

name: Sara Balaban
text:
I just got back from SYB's Palawan, Philippines Island-hopping adventure, and out of the 7 SYB trips I've taken so far, this one just snagged my number 1 spot. The Philippines with SYB feels like a secret people desperately need to know about. First off, leaders Lizzie and Ryan were phenomenal, and the smaller group allowed for deep connections and community, something we are all craving. Even better? No cell service for 5 days, was the gift I had been yearning for. I was able to be present and appreciate the beautiful surroundings and real-time conversations with really awesome people. Sleeping in beach huts was an amazing experience, and considering we were sleeping mostly on private island with just our group, the bathroom situation was totally fine. (coming from a girl living in the upper east side of NYC).  Honestly, it was so freeing not worrying about what I was wearing or how my hair looked, because we were living in swim suits and in the ocean all day snorkeling, kayaking, or getting sandy during yoga and beach workouts. This trip is the epitome of a 'primal reset," - everything that SurfYogaBeer stands for: community, wellness, connection, mindfulness. If you need a digital detox, love boat days, the ocean, the freshest organic food, beach games, dancing under the stars, and want to experience the best trip of your life....SurfYogaBeer Philippines is a MUST!

PS: we had a jack russell puppy on our boat for the week, which was a HUGE added bonus.

name: Cole Untiedt
text: Surf Yoga Beer is the best group travel out there! Everything is handled and communicated to you ahead of time, and you are introduced to the group. name: Austin Caldwell
text:
It’s not easy to describe the SYB Japan trip I just took, but to do so in one sentence is to say that it truly is lightening in a bottle - and something I definitely will keep with me my entire life.

The execution of logistics, for starters, is unparalleled. Our trip leader, Sarah, left no detail unturned. From the welcome dinner, I felt immediate connections to people who I know I’ll call friends for life. Book an SYB trip. It’s your best chance at capturing lightening in a bottle. Your only regret will be not booking one sooner.

name: Joey Valentino
text:
This trip to Nicaragua with Surf Yoga Beer was unreal. I’ve always been a solo, digital-nomad type traveler, but this completely sold me on group travel. Not lying, I’ve never smiled so hard, laughed so loud, trained so hard hungover, caught so many waves, and straight up never drank this much beer in my life 🤣

I’m not a great surfer, I hate yoga, and circuit training isn’t my thing but pushing my comfort zone with people I genuinely liked made it ridiculously fun. Seeking discomfort turned into the best part of the trip. I nailed the beer part too ;-)

Huge shoutout to Kaia, our group leader. She led with fun and adventure without ever feeling bossy or “in charge.” It was more like, damn… she’s got everything handled. She partied with us, but behind the scenes she was constantly managing logistics and adapting to changes so smoothly that we barely noticed when things didn’t go exactly as planned. I notice these things cuz I’m normally the one doing that.

What impressed me most: she took thousands of photos, narrowed them down to the best 600, edited them, and delivered everything in a Dropbox within a day and a half after the trip ended. That almost never happens. The photos are one of the best parts of experiences like this, and she absolutely crushed it.

Also shoutout to Brycen for being an incredible right-hand man always moving fast, helping wherever needed, and killing it on the camera while literally being the best at making everyone feel welcomed and comfortable. Like when I first arrived this dude was so warm and welcoming I was like hell yea. Thanks bro. Brycen ur the frikkin man. U inspire me bro.

Would 100% do this again.

name: Travis Hughes
text:
I approached SYB from a pretty big place of apprehension. Never had I solo-tripped before, and never had I flown into such a far away place not even being able to speak the local language. Were the people going to be my speed? Would I be the oddball that didn’t fit into this kind of group? What the hell am I doing?

Within about 24 hours with this group in the majesty of Nicaragua, not only were those questions quelled, but the answers were far more impactful on me than I ever could’ve realized. I have lifelong friends from such vastly different walks of life than my own, simply because we were all in the same boat looking for the same thing… but not even able to describe what we were looking for.

This came down to not only the people that booked the trip with me, but our leaders, Bradford and Kaia. At one point, we asked how long they had been doing this trip together, because everything, including a few unavoidable hiccups (nobody’s fault!) were handled with such grace and attention. Surely, these two had led dozens of these together. But nope, this was Kaia’s first trip after finishing SYB’s Leadership Academy. What a testament to her, and what a testament to all of SYB’s leaders for being able to set such a high standard! I’m confident that any trip would have this high level of leadership.

I could ramble on about what these folks, leaders, place, and event means to me. My biggest advice: the more nervous you are about a trip with SYB, the more you SHOULD book it. Trust me. You’ll get more out of it than folks who have done multiple.

Thanks so much for the trip of a lifetime, everyone!

name: Ashley Casper
text:
I found SYB while searching for "solo together" group trips. I wanted to travel, but felt intimidated doing it completely alone, and thought it would be more fun with people. From the very first WhatsApp message, SYB treated me like a person, not a number. They were responsive, encouraging, and went above and beyond to help me figure out flights and packing when I signed up on short notice for the Nicaragua surf camp.

That same level of care carried through the entire trip. Arrival and the border crossing were very new experiences for me but SYB paired us with buddies and had guides helping every step of the way. Once there, the accommodations were total vacation vibes: clean rooms with ocean views, infinity pools, cozy places to lounge, early morning coffee (I love coffee) and easy access to the beach. The onsite cooking and cleaning staff were friendly and professional, and the meals were delicious with lots of variety. I compared it to having tropical Thanksgiving. Our fearless SYB leaders took the best care of us, and having professional photographers meant we got to live in the moment, which I really appreciated.

Despite it being a surf camp, I didn’t know how to surf and went in fully prepared to just enjoy the beach instead. But the instructors were patient, adapted to all levels, and my group was incredibly encouraging. Everyone in our group ended up standing up on their surf board on day one, including me, (apparently a SYB first), which became a pretty perfect metaphor for the week — I kept trying things even if they were outside my comfort zone, and got lots of support along the way.

What surprised me the most though was the sense of community. A lot of trips promise connection but you never really know whether you'll make friends that last after the trip. Somehow, between all the activities, laughs, and shared experiences, this trip created space for genuine conversations in a way I've rarely .. maybe never ... experienced, even having done a lot of meetup events in the US.

The trip was operationally everything you'd want - it was well planned, fun, beautiful, and exciting - AND it also created space for real, meaningful connections.

name: Miles P. DeBole
text:
Surf Yoga Beer is a soul recalibration, disguised as a really good time. Lean in with me here for a minute:

I went on their January 2026 Nicaragua adventure.  This is the kind of excursion that changes you if you let it.

You wake up smiling. You go to bed smiling.
Then you hit 🔂

Everything hums:

•The place: grounding, wild, and rooted in the spirit of Nicaragua

•The community: open, curious, safe, welcoming, and kind

•The food: nourishing, abundant, and made with love

•The views: the kind that quiet your nervous system

•The itinerary: paced, well thought through, organized, and they know how to execute

•The surf: accessible no matter your level, playful, humbling, and pure joy

•The coffee: elite-tier

•The yoga: soulful, steady, living (again no matter your level)

•The vibes: dialed. always. somehow. You’ll feel this more than you can understand it

But the real magic? The leadership.

Kaia and Bradford are one of those rare combinations that make you glad you’re alive. They were our SYB guides.

They are endlessly fun, deeply loving, and completely attuned to energy — not just noticing it, but guiding it. They know when to turn the volume up, when to soften the room, when to let things unfold, and when to gently steer the ship. That kind of awareness isn’t taught. It’s embodied.

And here’s the thing that makes it unstoppable: They’re also consummate operators.

Everything just… FITS. Seamlessly. Effortlessly. Quietly. You feel held without ever feeling managed. Supported without being smothered. Free without chaos. That balance is rare — and it’s intentional.

Their warmth carries you exactly where you need to be — sometimes literally, always energetically.

They lead with joy, precision, integrity, and an unshakable commitment to their values. When belief and action are that aligned, it’s magnetic.

Arrived solo. Left with lifelong friends. Sarah, Ash, T3, Danny D, thank you for completing something in me I didn’t know I needed: a few crabs in a bucket 🦀🫠

Can only pray the spirit of Nica follows me home — gently but permanently: I know I’ll never be the same.

SO! If you’re still reading this, please, do yourself a favor.

“Buy the damn concert tickets!!” 🌊✨🍻

Mad love!
Miles

Aka MGK was on a training course during our trip and stuck it out with heart and maturity despite turning his ankle!! Can’t wait to watch you evolve, grow and master your craft through the journey SYB will provide my dude!! You’re a natural 💟

name: Katherine Moncrief (Kat)
text:
I just wrapped the SYB Ireland '25 trip, and it was everything I could've hoped for (and more) as a solo, social traveller. Our week moving across the country was a great balance of challenging physical activity, breathtaking sightseeing, authentic local immersion, and deep human connection. It was an adventure that I never could've designed for myself, and I'm so grateful to SYB for magic magic feel totally accessible.

I'd leave the review with a good ol' SYB "Don't think, just do!" and tell you to book right now if you're even thinking about it. But, if you're like me and you crave details, here's a bit more to tip you over the edge!

The Workouts: We did varied and challenging forms of exercise, which felt natural to our setting (Ireland = hiking, surfing, outdoor yoga, beach running) and were designed to push us out of our comfort zones. But we had the support of our team every time, which made everything -- even, in my case, hiking your first mountain -- possible. SYB is designed to let you focus on people, places, and pushing yourself, and not...

The Logistics: Book the trip, book your flights, and SYB takes care of the rest. It's really that easy! Our SYB leaders guided us through a thoughtful, packed schedule, and had arranged nice local hotels, an incredible bus driver, and quality food along the way. We really got  to "clock out" of planning for ourselves and "clock in" to that magic planned for us. Speaking of which...

The Plans: Ireland was the perfect balance of tourist -- the Guinness Factory, Temple Bar, the Cliffs of Moher -- and off the beaten path -- hiking Carrauntoohil, surfing Lahinch beach, head-banging in a Killarney pub to Zombie, yoga in an abandoned monastery. We checked the typical boxes, so it felt like we really "did" Ireland, but focused on immersing in both the nature and the culture of the place. And all of this was thanks to...

The Leaders: Ireland was run by a group of clear-eyed, full-hearted, creative leaders. Bradford and Dan were just extraordinary. At any given time they were coaches, teachers, cheerleaders, guides, party starters, and sometimes therapists -- you name it, they did it. We also had an incredible photographer in Matas, who allowed us to be off our phones and in every moment. If you see any of these guys running an SYB, book it! They will do a great job with you and...

The People: Trips like SYB are self-selecting for people who travel the same way: fun, flexible, social, and with a bit of spice. No surprise, then, that the squad on this Ireland trip was "the craic"! I feel like I quickly made real, lasting friendships from all over, made possible only by SYB. That's not just the icing on the cake, it is the cake.

So, I'll summarize the review the same way I started it: If you're considering an SYB trip, don't think and just do! Friends, magic, and adventure await!

I’ve had friends recommend that I travel to Iceland with a group of friends where we rent a car and drive around the country. While that is a cheaper option than the package Surf Yoga Beer offers, I doubt myself (and other friends) would be able to plan a detailed, well thought out trip as well as Surf Yoga Beer did. All of my friends who did Iceland admitted they never hiked one of its famous trails (Fiimmvorouhals), or they hiked half of it. Surf Yoga beer planned an overnight hike where we trekked 16 miles to see incredible views shown below. text:
I went on the Egypt trip in April. I have mixed feelings. The group of people who traveled along were great. We all got along quickly and felt comfortable enough around each other to act silly. Our egyptian translators and guides were outstanding. I was excited to have a photographer and videographer on board, especially because my phone camera lens cracked right before my departure flight. We had many bumps along the way, which I expected in a third world setting.

Night 1- two of the women rooming together had angry, loud male hotel staff wake them up in the middle of the night. They were scared to death and were repeatedly told to get out of their room. They were super aggressive towards the two. Then was told it was a “misunderstanding, wrong room.” Eli (leader) was alerted of this in the morning and made promises to get their room comped or to buy them a bottle of liquor. Neither happened.

Our travel day to Luxor was expected to be long. However, a dust storm caused the highway to close down. So our 3 hour trip turned into 5+ due to the back roads and our bus breaking down multiple times. We made the best of it as i said, third world country- cut them some slack. Eli unsolicitedly told us that he was going to buy us all a spa treatment to make up for it. I was like, dang, that’s pretty cool and got excited for my treat. When the time came, we did not get spa treatments. I was let down.

We went to the Valley of the Kings and were told that seeing King Tut was extra. Then Eli said, “it’s on me.” Trying to be our hero and savior. Looking at our itinerary- it was included in the trip and it appears that the original plan of the day was to up charge us.  The sites were remarkable. Our balloon tour was cancelled due to weather. Nobody made a peep about it and Eli again started promising, “I’m going to make it up to you guys.” Lol, no one asked.

The boat was really fun and we got to relax a bit. We did get to parasail and wakeboard. Those were added to “make things up to us.” Meanwhile, none of us asked for these additional things, nor, did we expect them. Eli was constantly trying to please us with his offerings that he ultimately wouldn’t follow through on. I’d prefer honesty because he kept getting my hopes up. Looks like the going rate for hot air balloons over Luxor is around $80. Parasailing: $5-$15, wakeboarding: around $15. Not to nickle and dime but… here we are. The snorkeling was fabulous and the water was the clearest i have ever experienced. We were supposed to go squid fishing but were never reminded of it. I began to believe we were just cutting costs left and right for personal take home…
…TBC in photos (not enough characters to get the picture painted).

Highlights:

Croatia: lots of group workouts, big parties, boat day on a massive pirate ship, kayaking, crystal clear waters, the hotel has a lovely sauna and spa facility, I made so many new friends on this trip! Definitely a big trip for partying but also lots of good workouts and meditation and moments of connection with others.

Turkey: You're on a really deluxe boat the whole time. There is a chef who makes you the best multi-course turkish meals for 3 meals a day, the cabins have nice showers and AC, I slept out under the stars on the day-beds most nights just because I could, we swam in the sea multiple times a day, went water-skiing/wake boarding/jet skiing, did a bunch of hikes to points with stunning views of the Turkish coastline, went clubbing in Marmaris and Bodrum with 9 of my new best friends.

Lowlights:
Going back to work/school after such a magical 3 weeks. Can't wait to go on my next SYB trip - hopefully one of the ones to Nicaragua so I can get my surf on!

About the company: I learned about SYB through Instagram ads and wondered how the actual experience would compare to the ads... I have to say it delivered exactly what was advertised. The boat in the ads was the boat we were on, the people in the ads and the quality of those photos is what they deliver with their professional photographers taking pictures of everyone all day every day. text:
Spent a week with SYB in Croatia and had a blast. Loved the workouts, camaraderie and meeting lots of like minded people. Really loved Steph & Mantis’ energy and how they balance each other. The Deep convos were my favorite. As with most group trips (or anything in life) it’s what you make of it. If you want a trip to spend your time on a bender you could do that; or if you wanted to just focus on early mornings, workouts and sightseeing you could do that too. The group was pretty accommodating.

Generally, I’d very much consider going on another trip with less people. It’s really hard to get to know 40+ people in a week; but regardless still a worthwhile adventure.

My major gripe was why bother flying in a DJ if the person is not going to do their job and focus more on fraternizing with the clientele? (That’s the kindest way I can put it). Numerous times we were left at the events with zero DJ at the booth and someone else focusing on the playlist. Seems like a waste of time and frankly entirely unprofessional / low integrity behavior. My advice: find someone who can be a professional and whose focus and passion is DJing. Not this charlatan we had. I won’t go into further details publicly.

Besides that as I said, you can make the trip whatever your heart desires. Want to relive spring break in college? Feel free. There’s a few folks who did that. Want to focus more on being an adult? Room for that too. All were welcome. The senior staff (Mantis, Steph) plus Chuks, Sam & Darryl did a great job shepherding us around Croatia. Will likely try a smaller group to see how the dynamics work out (I’ve been on many group tours in the past with other operators) and genuinely enjoyed this trip. With a few tweaks I think this trip could be spectacular.

name: Alex Harasty
text:
1. Destination / Activities

The location for home base on the Amalfi coast was perfect — the little fishing village we stayed in was beautiful and made it feel like we had the whole place to ourselves. The hotel staff even came out to party with us a couple nights even as they scolded us in the morning for being too rowdy in the lobby. We did manage to do the most important touristy things (Pompeii) but in a way that got us to skip lines and any logistical hurdles involved with 50,000 people trying to stampede their way through a 2000 year old archeological dig. The only hesitation you should have with anything on the trip is, if you get motion sick, get as much dramamine and motion sickness patches into your suitcase as you can. The roads are narrow, winding, and mountainous, and the water in the Mediterranean can be as choppy as it is beautiful.

2. Workouts

As a fitness coach who does not usually traffic in high fives and upbeat vibes, I was concerned that my generally surly approach to exercise was going to keep me from enjoying the workouts. Admittedly, I was a little drunk for the first one, but Mantas’ combination of soul cycle / functional fitness put me at ease right away. Be warned - if he says that the hike is just ‘a little walk’, don’t believe him, prepare for war. As for the yoga, even if you never end up on a SYB trip, you should absolutely find a way to take a yoga class with Molly.

3. Leaders

Of all the solo travel companies out there, this is really where SYB cannot be matched. Steph’s ability to sense the energy of the group, decide whether it needs a pick me up, and still keep track of all the tasks needed to keep 40 people fed/transported/housed is absolutely staggering. There isn’t a lunch table in the world where she couldn’t sit down and immediately make everyone else around her feel more comfortable with themselves or sharing parts of themselves with near strangers. Mantas, despite probably sleeping the least, exercising the most, and still having to run the rest of the business during the trip never showed a single sign of fatigue or frustration. Chuko took the 3 best photos of me ever taken. Molly went from a total stranger to giving me some of the most needed life advice I have ever received in the course of 3 days. If you trust nothing else from SYB, trust that the people in charge of your trip will be people you’ll admire and be a better person having met them.

name: Meag Donnelly
text:
I found out about SurfYogaBeer through a fitness instructor in Boston, MA in 2021. I entered an Instagram giveaway for $500 off of a trip to Greece at the end of August and won. I had never traveled anywhere out of the U.S. alone + wouldn't know anyone on the trip. As a single young female, I was a bit anxious to go but SYB made allll of my worries go away immediately - I had a call with one of their leaders, Steph, who is to this day one of the most welcoming people I know, who gave me the low-down on what to expect, what to pack, and if anyone in my area was also going. I connected with someone on the trip who had the same connecting flight as me, and they grouped us by arrival time so that we didn't have to travel to Athens alone. The trip itself was nothing short of unreal. We sailed the Aegean sea to four unreal islands over a span of 7 days in a fleet of four 40-foot catamarans (once in a lifetime opp right there) and headed back to Athens to learn about this history of the city on our last days. The energy we felt when we first met our group in SYB was electric - so welcoming, so helpful, all so excited to get to know one another -most of us coming on our own. I hadn't done much working out before I came to SYB, and I was met with encouragement, tips, modifications, and pride at our workouts - there truly is a space for everyone there. I loved SYB so much that I went on another trip at the end of 2022 to their New Year's in Nicaragua - a country that is incredibly underrated, where the food is fresh, and the people are so kind- not to mention, the beach is unreal. I was unsure I'd be able to recreate that sense of community we did in Greece or if it was a one-time fluke, but again, I was met with energy, inclusion, excitement, and still to this day talk to (and call some of my closest friends) the people I met in Greece and Nicaragua. I will continue to go on trips with SYB and shout to the rooftops to whoever will listen : Don't Think, Just DO! You will not regret it.
If you're looking for a change of pace, want to find a community, see a new spot and your friends just won't book the ticket, SYB is the perfect place for you.

name: Brian Schulz
text: Sailed around The Philippines' Palawan Islands for a week making pit stops to recharge, refuel + reinvigorate the mind, body + soul. name: Nathalie Jolain
text:

name: Dennis Ren
text: Easily the funnest week of my life! Every activity was perfectly curated with plenty of downtime in between - hidden local only places that I wouldn't have been able to find or plan on my own. Best part.....30 other like minded strangers that become life long friends by the end of the trip!

name: Amal
text:
Not your average fitness adventure trip. Do yourself a favour and go for one. I did 3 so far and can confirm SYB knows how to create magic, throw parties, and bring together amazing people.
Booking was always super easy, and also flexible: you may pay only a deposit and use it towards a different trip later if your plans change. Once confirmed, you get a booklet with a lot of information from recommended routes to get to the location to useful phrases in the local language you may need to navigate your way. The crew is always thoughtful and well prepared, having run these trips for almost 10 years. I’d almost say they knew the places more than locals. Leaders are hand picked - all super fun, inspiring, energetic individuals and party animals (some of which have their own workout plans, communities, retreats), including a professional photographer/videographer. Every trip has its own program depending on the location. Expect plenty of movement - there won’t be any missed opportunity to workout -, unlimited alcohol, parties you won’t forget as well as space for self reflection and sharing. What make these trips most special are the friendships you walk away with. Active adventures in off the beaten paths only attract cool, easy going, positive people. There’s no particular age range, the groups in the trips I took were quite mixed, mostly mid twenties to early forties I’d say, and everyone was young and wild at heart. Many who did previous SYB trips come back for more (you're warned!)
The Remote trip in Nicaragua was a highlight amongst the ones I went for. We were a small, close knit group and planned our schedule to fit our individual work commitments. I can’t think of a better setting to create new habits, get to know like minded people, and do plenty of activities alongside working. We did journal, meditate, workout, surf then have breakfast, all before logging in for work at 9.30am. Food was fresh, varied and wholesome. The place we stayed at was an absolute hidden gem, with all the facilities you’d need in life (pools, yoga deck, gym) and unreal sunset views. It couldn’t have been more perfect.
Thank you Mantas, Steph and SYB team!

name: Kelly-Anne
text: Just got back from one month in Nicaragua with SYB and I'm already going through major withdrawals! To say that it was a life changing experience would be an understatement - from day one I felt like I had found a new home. Everyone was so open, excited, and positive. The accommodations were great, the food was delicious, and the workouts/ activities had me (happily) exhausted  every night. 12/10 would recommend!

name: VICTORIA ZANCA
text: As a woman, traveling internationally can be scary but not with Surf Yoga Beer! I felt completely safe navigating airports. They arranged and accommodated all rides with trusted friends! This was my first time traveling international and I felt so welcomed by all of the Surf Yoga Beer leaders that greeted me with a warm smile and a nice cold beer of course! I fell in love with the experience of meeting like minded people who share the same interest and who genuinely have a passion for fitness and a healthy life style. Nicaragua was the first destination I booked for the New Years Eve trip because my friend Erinn just so happens to be the photographer for the company and she would be there. While on my stay I learned how to surf, zip line through the jungle, and practice yoga with the most epic view of Playa Maderas. Having this experience and making friends who are all just going through life exactly like you, is an experience unlike anything else. I will forever remember and cherish these moments. A special thank you to Julianna, SYB leader and yoga instructor on the trip who was readily available from the time of arrival and who lead the BEST yoga classes. A special thank you to Stephanie, SYB leader for going out of her way to help me in any way possible to make sure I was comfortable the entire trip. A special thank you to Mantis, Mike, and Duncan for having such exceptional leadership skills and making this trip so memorable. If you’re considering booking a trip, adopt the SYB mindset of  “don’t think, just do” and you might just see me on your next vacation!

text: This was my first SYB trip (Nicaragua) and I can't wait for the next in a few months! name: Svetlana
text:
All you need to know: I have been home less than three weeks since my SYB New Year’s trip in Nicaragua, and I have already booked my next SYB trip this summer - alongside 10 others from the same trip! It is an UNREAL experience – there is this inexplicable combo of fitness, fun and pure energy – you leave fully recharged both physically and mentally, with LOADS of memories and new friends.

Joining SYB trip was probably my best decision of 2022. I joined two days before it started and the trip over-delivered on so many levels.

Team. Mantas, Steph, Shriner, Juliana, Erinn – from the first message on Instagram to the last minute of the trip, they made sure to give 100% of themselves to make it an epic experience for everyone while having fun themselves and making it look so easy to run this (ultimate level of professionalism and experience).

People. Talk about a chance to meet diverse, kind and amazing personalities. People make the trip – and you will be going home with a set of new friends for life. I am very jealous though that a lot of people in my group live in the US and continue hanging out post-trip #fomo. BUT - already have some of the reunions planned in Europe and clearly, need to start planning a road-trip in the US:)

Itinerary. The true living of “surf, yoga, beer” name each day. I pretty much felt like I lived 5 days in one day – you manage to do a workout, a swim, a yoga, chill on the beach, do a surf lesson and still have energy to party throughout the night. Wig party, boat day, karaoke night – I really don’t know how it all fits just in one week!

VIBE. I can’t explain it – it is just so “warm”. Don’t think, just book the trip and experience it yourself!

name: Nicolas ansara
text: All I can say is WOW Kenya. I’m still day-dreaming about this trip and what a wild and incredible adventure that it truly was.  For their first trip to Kenya all of my expectations were blown out of the water. The trip started off on a high note for me, by having the opportunity to get up close and personal with giraffes and lions while feeding them out of my hands! The experiences only elevated from there! From riding bicycles through Hell’s Gate, taking our land rovers off-roading to chase down cheetahs and leopards, to an epic sunrise Hot air balloon safari over the Maasai Mara. Just to name a few. But one of my favorite things about an SYB trip are the people you meet along the way.  This trip took 19 strangers, dropped then off in Africa, and turned them into friends that will last a lifetime.  I cannot wait for the next SYB adventure!

name: Cezary Wójcik
text:
I think of a great travel experience in two parts -- to put it in the universal language of sandwich, the bread and the filling. And the SYB Kenya trip was a hell of a sando.

You can't have a sandwich without the bread (lettuce wrapped is no longer a sandwich). In travel, I see the bread as the destination, the sights, the experiences. Kenya was incredible. We saw lions and cheetahs and zebras up close in the wild in a way to which no zoo can ever compare. We flew over the Masai Mara in a calming and beautiful air balloon ride at sunrise. And we got our sweat on together any time we could by the poolside or in the courtyard while confused onlookers were wondering what the hell we were doing.

The filling of the sandwich, however, is the people with whom you share these experiences. It's the little moments in between all of the adventuring and sightseeing created purely by the people you're with, like vibing out to the Lion King soundtrack while 4x4ing between leopard sightings. It's spending time with people reveling in the moment and thrilled by the memories yet to be made. It's the realization of the idea that no matter where in the world you are or where you're from, we're all just human beings who are meant to enjoy things together. That's where the sandwich really gets its flavor, and that's a big part of what makes SYB so special. A group united from a combination of extended community and shared interests that starts as mostly strangers and ends as a team.

name: Z CHAI
text:
It is scary for anyone to travel to a foreign country with a group of people you have never met before. But, after that first introduction at the airport, thanks to SYB, it wasn’t long until we all felt embraced, cared for, challenged, and appreciated.

When I think about saying thank you to SYB, I don’t know where to start. It’s hard to put into words how much this company has had a positive impact on my life. SYB is a place to get fit, have fun, be vulnerable, find your limits (then surpass them), discover yourself, ditch your toxic relationships back home, and establish a new healthy mindset. SYB is an attitude and a lifestyle. If you haven’t signed up and experienced it yet, you are truly missing out.
SYB Iceland, thank you from the bottom of my heart; you have given me much more than a unique traveling experience. The positive outlook, influence, empathy, and courage of the leaders - @liamjaris, @aubreylauryn, @danidellarco, @tinadaq, and @aaroncolussi - are the linchpin of this experience. It quite simply can’t be replicated elsewhere. #takemeback #sybiceland

name: Jonathan Wexler
text:
Yoga: 5
Goats: 4
Beer: 1
Hiking: 4
Price: 1
Transportation: 2
Food: 2
Friendliness: 5

For the price, the experience felt poorly planned. Beer should not be considered part of the experience if it means arriving at a bar to spend more money on top of what was paid.

Deli sandwiches, inconveniently mixing vegan and meat sandwiches, with no water or drinks for lunch, felt like a last second lunch plan.

Bumpy yellow school bus for 1.5 hours each way. You’ll need another yoga session once you arrive home.

Goat caretakers and yoga instructor were professional and offered a fun engagement. SYB should have planned this event better, set expectations, probably lowered the price otherwise, and provides more staff support.
